# Warning Complexity {background-color="#006DAE"}

## What statistically makes a good forecast

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Forecast Verification[^1]

-   Calibration: How well does the forecast match the observed
    frequency?

-   Sharpness: How confident are we in the forecast?

<!-- -   Accuracy: How good is our forecast accuracy based on scoring metrics? -->
:::

[^1]: Gneiting, T., & Katzfuss, M. (2014). Probabilistic forecasting.
    *Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application*, *1*(1), 125-151.

. . .

In practice there are other important factors, including timeliness and
the warning communication.

## Warning Value Chain

![](images/value_chain.png){width="100%"}

[^2]

[^2]: Hoffmann, D., Ebert, E. E., Mooney, C., Golding, B., & Potter, S.
    (2023). Using value chain approaches to evaluate the end-to-end
    warning chain. *Advances in Science and Research*, *20*, 73-79.

## Risk Framework

<center>![](images/IPCC_risk_framework.png){width="75%"} [^3]</center>

[^3]: Simpson, N.P. et al. (2022) ICSM CHC White Paper II: Impacts,
    vulnerability, and understanding risks of climate change for culture
    and heritage ...

# Data Barriers {background-color="#006DAE"}

## Impact Forecasts

:::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Natural hazard interact with people's social and personal contexts

::: incremental
-   The same hazard will impact people differently
-   People also interpret risk from the same hazard differently
-   People need access to different information to understand their
    impacts
-   Indirect impacts from a hazard can still be life threatening
    <!-- -   People respond to warnings differently based on their own personal perception of risk -->
:::
::::

## What data?

<br><br>

::: callout-caution
## Take a moment to brainstorm

What are the different types of data you might want if you were issuing
a warning?

Who might be the different organisation involved in issuing a warning and how might they need to share data?

:::

## Impacts

:::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Broad variety of impacts that intersect with someone socio-personal context

::: incremental
-   Service utility outages [(eg. Water, sewerage, power, phone,
    internet.)]{style="color:gray;"}
-   Transport outages [(eg. Road closures , public transport outages,
    disruptions and outages of rideshare
    services.)]{style="color:gray;"}
-   Emergency services [(eg. Changed access to police, fire,
    ambulance.)]{style="color:gray;"}
-   Other essential services [(eg. Changed access to healthcare,
    hospitals, pharmacies, and supermarkets, including supply
    disruptions.)]{style="color:gray;"}
-   Support services [(eg. Changed access to supports for mental health,
    domestic violence, and drug and alcohol
    abuse.)]{style="color:gray;"}
:::
::::

. . .

We need interoperable data to understand how the hazard impacts

## Data barriers

:::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
::: incremental
-   Too many of our important data sets are behind pay walls

-   Where possible data should be open for shared use

-   Sometimes data is open but there is no existing pipeline or
    mechanism to use it

-   This might mean it is not machine readable, its in propriety formats
    and not interoperable

-   The data is often not maintained or updated so is not fit for
    purpose
:::
::::

## 

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
NSW Hazard Watch ![](images/nsw_hazard_watch.png){width="88%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Vic Alert ![](images/vic_vicalert.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Avoiding data silos

Natural disasters do not adhere to institutional remits or geographic
borders!
:::

## Gold Standards in Data Science

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## FAIR principles

-   **F**indable - **A**ccessbile - **I**nteroperable - **R**eusable
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## 5-star data

-   Appropriate license (Ideally Open!)
-   Machine-readable, structure format
-   Non-propriety formats
-   Digital Ojbect Identifier (Can be cited)
-   Links to other datasets
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
We also need meta-data!
:::

## 

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Many warnings are not reproducible

If data disappears it is difficult to evaluate if warnings were reliable and
sufficient to act upon

:::

<center>![](images/20220228_Brisbane_River_Flood_Forecast_map_4_0m_AHD.png){width="80%"}</center>

## 

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Need to get our data talking!

Then we can have improved, more user-centric warnings
:::

<center>![](images/datasolve.jpg){width="85%"}</center>

## Data equity 

<br><br>

:::callout-caution
## Breakout discussion: Time to think 

Some regions in Australia are better observed and have better data.

What should the government's policy be on warning communication: 

Should warnings be standardised statewide, or should some communities with better data have more detailed user-centric warnings?

:::

. . .

:::{.callout-caution appearance="minimal"}
## Speaking of equity 

In designing digital warning infrastructure, do we need to consider any specific community needs?

:::

# Data Innovation {background-color="#006DAE"}

##  {background-image="images/kayak2.jpg"}

::: {.callout-tip style="background-color: white;"}
## Reminder: Why do we need open data ...

Open data has the ability to transform government businesses and society. 

:::

## 

:::{.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
## Open data allows us to build tools to solve problems in society
:::

<center>
![](images/watch_duty.png){width="75%"}
</center>

[Guardian News Article](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jan/05/watch-duty-wildfire-app)

[Watch Duty Website](https://www.watchduty.org/)

## 

:::{.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
## Open data allows us to fact-check mis-information and dis-information
:::

:::{.callout-caution appearance="minimal"}
## Were the 2020 bushfires caused by arson? The answer is no!  

Open data helped us to understand - see [analysis submitted to UNDRR](https://www.preventionweb.net/news/open-data-shows-lightning-not-arson-was-likely-cause-most-victorian-bushfires-last-summer#:~:text=Open%20data%20shows%20lightning%2C%20not,can%20be%20attributed%20to%20arson.), [R Spotoroo Package](https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2023-022) and [Geoscience Australia Hotspot data](https://hotspots.dea.ga.gov.au/)

:::

<center>
![](images/fire_causes.png){width="75%"}
</center>

## 

:::{.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
## Open data can also helps us to understand where we have knowledge gaps
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Current data

Large gaps in our observing network

Temporal frequency of data may be lower than the evolving hazard

Often don't know the on the ground conditions
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## For higher resolution data in space and time we need cultivate, novel data sources

-   Crowd-sourced weather data

-   Crowd-sourced text, photos and videos (drones)

-   Crowd-sourced reporting ([road closures](https://www.waze.com/discuss/t/external-data-third-party-sources-policy/375445), environment)
:::

## A comment

:::{.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Government led innovation can be slow
:::

. . . 

:::{.callout-caution appearance="minimal"}
## Question

Can you think of why that might be? 

:::

# Wrap Up {background-color="#006DAE"}

## Perspective Paper Recommendations

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Going forward

1.  Work towards open, FAIR data and transparent models, particularly
    for hazard and impact forecasts

2.  Adhere to best practices in visualisation and appropriately
    integrate interactive elements

3.  Create data infrastructure so that novel data sources, like
    crowd-sourced data, can be used to support more localised warnings,
    and

4.  Better incorporate uncertainty into emergency decision-making,
    visualisation, and warning communication.
:::

## Calls for change

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Parliamentary Inquiry into the 2022 Flood Event in Victoria

-   Based on the data barriers discussed, a submission was made on 5th June 2023

:::

<small>

> *There are three key points raised in relation to:*

> *1. Adequacy of warning information available for the October flooding on the state border.*

> *2. Our ability to evaluate if warnings were indeed effective given the transparency of the data and transparency of information about the models used to produce the warnings.*

> *3. Our ability to evaluate adequacy of warnings in hindsight given the lack of reproducibility in the warnings and general storage of the data.*

</small>

## Takeaways

:::callout-note
## Summary

I want you to leave today: 

* With a deeper understanding for the societal importance of open data 

* Whether it be natural hazards, or something else, our world is complex!

* Data needs to works together seamlessly (adhere to data best practices!)

* Knowing the important role that open data plays in innovation

* Feel empowered to use open data to create change 

:::
